topic: Spider-Man: Homecoming — The Contract That Created The Vulture

beats.narration_text: You never asked why a New York salvage crew was holding alien weapons,
beats.scene_description: Extreme close-up of blue-collar crew slicing through alien Chitauri armor with a glowing extraterrestrial energy cutter.

beats.narration_text: and the answer is one cancelled contract.
beats.scene_description: Adrian Toomes supervising his salvage crew stacking alien armor plating under the Manhattan wreckage.

beats.narration_text: Spider-Man: Homecoming shows you this in its opening minutes and never says it out loud.
beats.scene_description: Child's crayon drawing of Avengers transitioning into the shattered skyline of Grand Central and Stark Tower debris.

beats.narration_text: After the Battle of New York, Adrian Toomes runs a salvage company hired to clean up the wreckage.
beats.scene_description: Heavy cranes, industrial haulers, and debris removal operations at the epicenter of the Battle of New York.
Multiple working-class laborers cutting metal and securing cargo; an authentic functioning local enterprise.

beats.narration_text: Then Damage Control, a government outfit with Stark's backing, takes the job over.
beats.scene_description: Sleek government vehicles and armed federal personnel arriving to seize control of the site.
Anne Marie Hoag issues executive order 396B, terminating the salvage contract on the spot.

beats.narration_text: Toomes is left with a warehouse of alien tech and a crew that still needs paying.
beats.scene_description: Back of the salvage truck reveals glowing purple Chitauri power cores and hoarded extraterrestrial salvage.

beats.narration_text: So he keeps the tech and builds weapons from it.
beats.scene_description: The Tinkerer soldering circuitry and testing high-powered alien blasters in the dimly lit warehouse workshop.

beats.narration_text: That's the answer: one lost contract.
beats.scene_description: Adrian Toomes emotional confrontation: 'I bought trucks for this job. I brought in a whole new crew. These guys have a family.'

beats.narration_text: The Vulture isn't chasing power, he's protecting a payroll.
beats.scene_description: Vulture exoskeleton wings lock onto Toomes' harness, glowing green optical sensors activate in the shadows.

beats.narration_text: Which Marvel villain had the most believable motive? Tell me in the comments.
beats.scene_description: The Vulture launches from the warehouse platform with twin jet turbines roaring into the night sky.
